leads.summary: Steam regression test passes even when its Lua assertions fail
leads.consequence: The bare `lua <<'LUA'` runs stdin as a REPL on the tested Lua 5.5.1 interpreter: a failed assert prints a traceback yet exits 0. Bash `set -e` continues to `pass`, and test/shell treats the broken file as passing. The pinned merge-base steam.lua run recorded both a `Steam main window keeps its floating rule` traceback and an `ok` result, overall exit 0; explicit `lua - <<'LUA'` changed that negative control to exit 1 and the head still exited 0. This permits the exact regression the test purports to catch; reruns remain false green. Use `lua -` to make failure propagate.

Its changes to other tests cannot fix this newly added call. leads.summary: Layout regressions still pass the Steam test even after its exit status is fixed
leads.consequence: The test only checks that a gamescope inhibitor rule exists, not that it has no `float`. Adding `float=true` to that rule (a plausible mistaken reuse of the client float rule) leaves the test green but floats gamescope; dropping Friends List's `size={460,800}` similarly leaves it green. Both verified with separate disposable mutants under review.py after changing `lua` to `lua -`. Add assertions that gamescope has no float, and that main/Friends List size and centering remain, separately from the exit-mode fix. Stubbed `hl.window_rule` also does not evaluate actual Hyprland matching or effects.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus secondary test notes (different mutants); omitted from public comment for proportion

leads.summary: Open #10123's Steam-window documentation becomes false if both PRs merge
leads.consequence: #10123 tells users that every Steam window floats and that re-tiling the main Steam client leaves login, Settings, Friends List and popups floating. With this PR the default float exists only for literal titles `Steam` and `Friends List`; a class-steam window titled `Sign in to Steam` or `Steam Settings` no longer has a Steam float rule. Its doc patch applied without rejection to a private copy of this head's manual, leaving the false claim at lines 41,47. Coordinate a docs update if #10123 merges, describing only main and Friends List floats and the actual behavior of other dialogs.

leads.summary: Borderless-only nested gamescope is outside the new fullscreen inhibitor
leads.consequence: On a nested gamescope 3.16.31 launch with `-b` but without `-f` and no additional compositor fullscreen override, its outer window has class gamescope but is not compositor-fullscreen. Hyprland's `idle_inhibit=fullscreen` requires actual fullscreen on a visible workspace, so a borderless game can still trigger Omarchy's idle screensaver and lock if no application-provided inhibitor is active. The gamescope source distinguishes -b from -f; its SDL backend sets BORDERLESS and FULLSCREEN_DESKTOP independently, and Wayland backend requests fullscreen only for its fullscreen mode. This is a conditional scope gap rather than proof that all borderless games are broken; if borderless use is intended, consider focus-mode inhibition for gamescope or explicitly scope the fix to actual fullscreen and test that edge.
leads.triage: behavioural hypothesis without runtime observation; Opus covers borderless generally as lower-weight note; dropped

leads.summary: Two open Steam idle-inhibit PRs overlap, their tests expect a rule this PR removes
leads.consequence: Open #9667 and #12114 are each diverged from this head, not stacked, and both add a narrow steam_app_.* fullscreen idle-inhibit rule to the old four-line steam.lua. `git merge-file` using each PR's own merge base produced conflict markers. Tested this reconciliation: this PR's corrected Steam test passes, #9667 and #12114 each fail at `the Steam client still gets a fullscreen idle inhibitor`. When merging, keep this PR's broad coverage and update/drop the narrow redundant rule and tests, rather than reintroducing blanket float just to satisfy literal assertions.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the new rules do what the description says. Hyprland 0.56.2 full-matches window-rule regexes, so `steam.*` covers `steam`, `steam_app_<id>` and other classes starting with `steam`. Fullscreen `steam_app_*` games, games reporting class `steam` (the Age of Empires II case from #6947) and `gamescope` windows get `idle_inhibit = "fullscreen"`. Class-`steam` games no longer receive an Omarchy float rule. The Steam main window keeps float, center and 1100x700, and the English Friends List keeps float and 460x800. The same holds with current `quattro`'s `helpers.lua`, since `o.window` is unchanged there.

Two points look worth addressing: the new test's assertions cannot fail it, and the float scoping also drops float from the other Steam client windows.

### The new test passes even when its assertions fail

`test/shell.d/steam-test.sh` runs `lua <<'LUA'` without a script argument. When stdin is not a terminal, the standalone interpreter runs the chunk, prints any error to stderr and still exits 0 (`lua.c` in 5.4 and 5.5). `set -euo pipefail` therefore never trips, and the script reaches `pass`.

| `steam.lua` under test | As written (`lua <<`) | With `lua - <<` |
|---|---|---|
| This PR | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| Merge-base rules | **exit 0**, prints `ok` (traceback: `Steam main window keeps its floating rule`) | exit 1 |
| Gamescope rule removed | exit 0 | exit 1 |
| Syntax error appended | exit 0 | exit 1 |

**Impact:** the regression test gives no protection. The `hyprland-default-config-test.sh` run cited in the description gives none for `steam.lua` either: it uses the same form and also exits 0 with a broken `steam.lua`.

**Suggested change:** `OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" lua - <<'LUA'`, the form `hyprland-paths-test.sh` and `hyprland-qconsole-test.sh` already use. Open #7460 adds `shell-test-style-test.sh`, which rejects any `lua <<` heredoc in `test/shell.d/`, so this file would fail that check as written.

### Other Steam client windows lose their float rule

The base floated every window whose class is exactly `steam`. At this head, `float = true` is only on the rules titled exactly `Steam` and `Friends List`. Float is a static effect, applied once when the window maps, using its title at that moment.

```text
class steam, title ...           base     this PR
Steam                            float    float
Friends List                     float    float
Lista de amigos (localized)      float    no Omarchy float rule
Steam Settings                   float    no Omarchy float rule
Sign in to Steam                 float    no Omarchy float rule
(empty title, reportedly menus)  float    no Omarchy float rule
```

This table models the rules against Hyprland's source. It was not measured in a live session.

**Impact:** without an Omarchy rule, Hyprland floats these windows only if its own heuristics apply (for example dialog or menu window types, transient parents, fixed size hints, override-redirect). Otherwise they tile. Whether Steam Settings or the sign-in window tile in practice was not observed. The class-wide float was a deliberate default (#759: "Not meant to tile, because it's just meant to be a launcher"), and the PR description frames the scoping around games without mentioning the other client windows.

**Suggested change:** check the client windows with `hyprctl clients -j` in a live session. Then either list the titles that should keep floating (titles are localized and must be set when the window maps), or keep the class-wide float and override the reported class-`steam` games. Otherwise, mention the change in the description.

**Related PRs:** open #9667 and #12114 also edit `steam.lua` (both add a `steam_app_.*` inhibitor next to the class-wide float) and conflict with this change. #9667's test also fails against these rules. Open #10123 proposes manual text saying Steam's login prompt, Friends List, Settings and popup menus keep floating, which relies on the class-wide float this PR removes.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the rule change against Hyprland 0.56.2 source (rule matching, static effects, idle inhibition). The PR test, the merge-base rules, diagnostic mutants and a `lua -` variant were run in a sandbox with Lua 5.5.1 (the exit-status behavior was also reproduced with Lua 5.4.9), and the effects on the windows above were evaluated from the loaded rules. No live Hyprland session, Steam client, game or gamescope was run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
